facts.detail: The GigaHubs Process Review was published on 26 June 2026.
Belmana authored the review and conducted the study with GC Insight for BDUK.
The evaluation runs from 2022 to 2027 and reviews GigaHubs delivery during 2021 to 2026.
The Hub product focused on remote public buildings including schools, GP surgeries and libraries.
The review uses BDUK management data and interviews with government, local authorities, suppliers and site representatives.

facts.detail: The technical annex was published on 26 June 2026.
The annex contains a data-and-modelling section and a case-study approach section.
The study used BDUK administrative data for 2,553 Hubs supported by the programme.
Seven administrative-data snapshots were collected between July 2023 and July 2024.
The England modelling combined 28,998 public buildings, including primary schools, GP surgeries and libraries.

facts.detail: The summary reports approximately 1,200 GigaHubs connections delivered during 2021 to 2026.
Delivery took place through six projects led by government, devolved and local-authority bodies.
The programme contributed to 5,670 Hubs delivered by BDUK as of September 2025.
The review found that the 100-site minimum limited the number of local authorities able to assemble viable projects.
Education had a clearer adoption pathway, while uptake in health and library settings was slower and more dependent on wider IT strategies.

facts.detail: The Theory of Change describes GigaHubs as part of the £5 billion Project Gigabit mission.
The report records £110 million of Project Gigabit funding as available for Hubs.
The product funded gigabit connections for rural schools, GP surgeries, libraries and other public buildings.
The model links Hub connections to improved public services and lower barriers for nearby homes and businesses.
The updated Theory of Change reports eligible sites declining from 4,603 in 2020 to 1,207 in 2022.

facts.detail: BDUK published the Local Full Fibre Network Evaluation Plan on 15 August 2025.
The page describes LFFN as a £200 million programme.
BDUK commissioned GC Insights, Belmana and Darren Kilburn to evaluate waves two and three.
LFFN aimed to stimulate commercial investment in gigabit-capable digital connectivity.
The evaluation is organised into six phased work packages covering programme delivery and impact.
